founder_acceptance.rationale: Two review campaigns, the cap, ran on a high-risk package (credentials, first data egress from the Mac, migration of real local data, an API semantics change). Campaign 1 raised 63 findings (2 blocking) and campaign 2 raised 65 (2 blocking); neither raised a product decision, and all 128 were fixed with none rejected (review-c1-disposition.md, review-c2-disposition.md). The verdict stayed technical-changes-required only because no third campaign is allowed to confirm the campaign-2 fixes. The owner accepts the residual risk that a fix is incomplete, chiefly in the legacy Mac import, bounded by the compensating measures below. Panel caveat: every lens ran through a Claude-backed adapter (ADR-0025 exception chosen by the owner) on one provider: campaign 1 used Sonnet 5.5 and Fable 5.1 with Opus 5.5 on UX; campaign 2 used Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 (the owner removed Fable for cost). Opus 5.5 also authored the spec and plan, so the panel is correlated and partly self-review; every lens is recorded as degraded and model-unverified.
compensating_measures: Every PR slice from tasks.md gets its own independent review and full CI before landing, per ADR-0008 and ADR-0023; ASK-class slices need the owner's recorded approval.
Each slice's PR description lists the review-c1/c2 dispositions it implements, so a reviewer can check that the planned fix actually landed in code.

Before the owner upgrades their own Mac, the legacy import is dry-run on a copy of the owner's real local data folder (quickstart Scenario 6 step 0, BRAINBUDDY_MAC_DATA_DIR override); the app never deletes the pre-upgrade backup.
/speckit-accept runs before release and maps every FR and SC to a named executable test or recorded host evidence with fresh Allure or tree-hash evidence; a reject verdict blocks the release.
The owner uses Mac, iPhone and web on one account for one week of normal work (SC-007) before the feature is called done.
If any slice changes spec.md, plan.md or a contract beyond the dispositions, that change gets a targeted review (Sonnet or Opus) instead of relying on this acceptance.
